quest.title: In the Shifting Light of the Moon
quest.description: The journey so far has reached a brief pause. Take a moment to rest and check in on your companions.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act V
chapter.title: A Nocturne of the Far North

talks.objective: Go to the Adventurers' Guild in Nasha Town

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Thank you for waiting. I've finished checking your Adventurer Handbook. Here are your commission rewards.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: We have no other urgent commissions on the books at present. Thank you for all your hard work lately. Perhaps you two could consider taking a vacation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Amazing! Paimon never thought we'd end up having down time in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Things were pretty hectic when we first got here. Everywhere you looked, it was either The Wild Hunt causing chaos or the Fatui stirring up trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It felt like this whole region was one giant slime-in-a-barrel, ready to go "boom" at any moment!

choices.text: We really have achieved a lot since we've been here, haven't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure have... Things were looking pretty dicey, but in the end we managed to turn it around. ...Whoa, Paimon just got deja vu... Oh, that's right — it's because we've done this, like, a million times now, hehe.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Ah, yes. Are you two aware that the Moon-Prayer Night is soon to take place?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Lauma told us that was coming up soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, why do you mention it, though? Do people in Nasha Town celebrate it too? Paimon thought it was just for Moon Goddess worshipers.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: You're partially right. Most people in Nasha Town just see the festival as an opportunity to do business. They do not concern themselves with the religious element.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The festival was first celebrated by the Frostmoon Scions. On this day, they would wear Moon-Prayer Blossoms and celebrate the birth of the Moon Goddess through song and dance.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: They would also prepare food and handicrafts, and give them as gifts to others. Over time, it became Nod-Krai's most lively festival.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, sounds like fun!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm definitely up for it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Hehe, well, in the meantime, since Katheryne doesn't have any commissions for us, let's focus on some personal business instead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When we first got here, you mentioned that this was where your spaceship landed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We didn't get to follow up on it at the time, 'cause we got wrapped up in that whole Rerir situation. But now, we can finally start investigating it properly!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Except, we have no idea where to start...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... There's a saying Paimon's heard around these parts, which goes: "If you lift up a rock, you'll find something you weren't looking for."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By that logic, you'll never find what you're looking for while you're searching, but the moment you stop looking, it'll jump right out at you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not sure it's as simple as that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could be worth a try though, right? Anyway, Paimon suggests we focus on other stuff we wanna do for now, and just keep an ear out for spaceship-related intel as we go.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We haven't seen Columbina in a while...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She used a huge amount of power in the final battle against Rerir, and has been much weaker since then.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I don't know if I can do anything to genuinely help her... but surely a little chat can do no harm.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (One other thing that concerns me is... We've seen no trace of The Doctor so far.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong? You look super serious all of a sudden.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I was just thinking about Columbina and The Doctor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Paimon gets why you'd be concerned about Columbina... But what does The Doctor have to do with anything?

choices.text: We learned back in Natlan that he's been investigating the moon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's true... And now that you mention it, we're definitely overdue for a showdown with the Fatui!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It is weird that he hasn't shown himself this whole time... What could he be up to?

choices.text: Engrossed in one of his experiments, perhaps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True. Paimon would much rather deal with Marionette, anyway. She says the meanest things, but when it comes down to it, she doesn't seem like a bad person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe it's the pressure of being a Fatuus? Especially as a harbinger. Does she feel like she's gotta act tough to keep up appearances or something?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Um... M—Maybe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But then, every time we had it out with Rerir, she always wound up having to repair Pulonia and her other robots.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's gotta sting... Losing face always hurts more for people who care a lot about their image. She's probably still furious about it...

choices.text: Uh, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Relax, she's not even here— Huh!?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: ...What's the matter?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, nothing, nothing. Sorry, we'll be on our way now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where were we, again? Oh yeah, Columbina? Right, yeah, let's go see Columbina, hehehe...

choices.text: I have a feeling she might've heard that.
Either way, his current inaction is a good thing.
But he's been suspiciously absent so far.
The Traveler and Paimon strike again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that's right! Another win for Teyvat's top duo!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, she's sitting up!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is me sitting here a rare sight?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No. We just thought you'd be resting.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps I would have been, were it not for the sudden arrival of some unexpected guests.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Not that I consider it a disturbance. After all, you are the only ones who are free to enter.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Would it not be a little unfriendly of me to lie down while we speak?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't realize you put so much thought into little things like that.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Only sometimes. There have been moments lately where I think about you and your companions.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They are warm, mysterious, and cozy memories. Very few of my past memories are anything like that.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...They say that travelers return home bearing bags full of souvenirs. But my luggage was empty, and I believed it would stay that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Return home...? So, you're still planning on returning to the moon...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. This planet continues to reject me, reminding me that I do not belong here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If I remain in Teyvat, there will come a day that I disintegrate. And I don't mean reduced to dust, or turned into food for the flowers. I mean, I will cease to exist entirely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then. Well, we're sure gonna miss you... but it sounds like we'll have to say goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you intend to return?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Moon-Prayer Night is soon to arrive. On that day, the moon will be closest to Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The kuuvahki in this land will reach its peak at that time. I merely need to grasp the tide, and with relatively little effort...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it. It'll work like a slingshot!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You make it sound like she's gonna get blasted up to the moon.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If I did that, I suspect I would crash into the false sky.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will be using a much gentler approach. But I do like the analogy. It's fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you see? She gets Paimon's sense of humor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In the blink of an eye, the time has come to part ways.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It does feel that way, doesn't it? Time seems to fly fastest when you are enjoying it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I have always thought of myself as a wanderer on this earth. And it has never expressed any desire to keep me here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yet just as I plan to depart, it tugs at my arm... Is this a gesture of affection, or is the world mocking me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh... Were you hoping I can answer that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. You are a Traveler, so you must have a lot of experience in this area.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then, what I would say is... enjoy the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Don't overthink it. Happiness is happiness, and joy is joy. The point is to enjoy it, not analyze it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I see. Then, what I would say is... even though I am very tired right now, I am still happy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't tell from the tone of your voice.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, really? You... don't think I sound happy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm just kidding. I could tell you were in a good mood today from the moment we saw you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah. A joke. Albeit not a funny one.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Anyway. I assume you're here about you-know-what? Give me your hand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, it's not that. There's something else we wanted to discuss with you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh. Then, do you still want to give me your hand, or not?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you. So, I've heard that in the Moon-Prayer Nights of the past, people here would hold celebrations in the Moon Goddess's honor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Since you helped so much in our fight against the Rächer of Solnari, I think you deserve a farewell party before you return home.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I haven't asked everyone else for their opinions on this yet, but I'd like to invite you to join the upcoming Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I've never joined a Moon-Prayer Night before. I'm not sure what I would even do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about that. We'd take care of everything! All you'd need to do is show up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course, there's no need to force it if you're not feeling strong enough. It's just, this kinda felt like a golden opportunity...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But, they call me Kuutar. And the Fatui have an arrest warrant out for me. I shouldn't appear in public right now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Yeah, there will definitely be complications... but...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll make it work. You have my word.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, we got your back! Well, {M#he}{F#she} does. Paimon's actually not too sure what {M#he's}{F#she's} planning...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Alright. If you're sure... I will not refuse your invitation.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I suppose it wouldn't hurt to pack a few more sights from this world into my suitcase before finally learning what my homeland looks like.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, if you see Lauma, please tell her that my answer to the question she asked me is neither "yes" nor "no."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Rather, it is "there is no need."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... That was kinda cryptic, but sure. Guess it's between the two of you. We'll pass along the message. Bye for now!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And also... I do not know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Lauma, it's us! ...Huh? Varka? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hahaha, beats me. I had a bit too much to drink last night, and when I woke up, I was on Hiisi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Mr. Varka is helping to oversee Nasha Town's preparations for Moon-Prayer Night. He is here to go over some details regarding the decorations and custom cloth designs.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Right, yeah. That too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "that too"!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, preparations are already underway?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. Celebrating this festival is a long-held tradition here in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: On this day, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance. Our people take these to be blessed omens.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's an especially welcome event coming off the back of all that nasty business with Rerir. Everyone got put through the wringer recently, and now they're looking to turn their fortunes around.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The big shots in town all agree that a big, lively celebration is just what we need to rebuild people's faith in this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder Katheryne said that people weren't so bothered about the religious element.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: That's right, it's become more of a local custom by this point. The celebrations have little to do with whether the religious stories behind this event are true or not.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Even the Frostmoon Scions are eagerly awaiting the coming of Moon-Prayer Night, despite now knowing that their past beliefs were founded on a falsehood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's fair. It's a bit like the Lantern Rite in Liyue. It's a chance for people to enjoy themselves, not debate the existence of the adepti.

choices.text: Although, in their case, the adepti definitely do exist...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, one other thing — we just went to see Columbina. We went ahead and invited her to take part in the festival this time. Hope that's okay.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Wait, so... You mean, she agreed to it? Huh. That's quite a surprise.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Then I suppose that she intends to return to the moon on that day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah. It's kind of a complicated process, but basically... Uh... It's like a slingshot!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She probably shouldn't have endorsed your metaphor...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I understand. Hm... In truth, I had a feeling that she might make such a decision.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Well, if Kuutar has decided to participate in the festival, we should prepare accordingly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, exactly! She was saying how it could be risky for her to show her face in public. We were wondering if there was any way we could hide her...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hmm... Unfortunately, the people who carved the statues did an excellent job of capturing her likeness. It will be very challenging to hide a goddess whose face everyone is so familiar with...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Darn. We may have bitten off more than we can chew here...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ah, don't sweat the small stuff! We can handle that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Are you saying you have a plan?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Not as such, no. But the most important thing with a festival is to keep the mood light and your spirits up.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You can't go preparing for a festival with those long faces. You'll never convince anyone to enjoy themselves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Mondstadter spirit is strong with this one...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: As it happens, I agree with Mr. Varka.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Let's start by making our appreciation for Kuutar the beating heart of the festive atmosphere.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: And who knows? Once we get the ball rolling, perhaps everything will just... fall into place?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Did you catch that? Lauma said the thing! Or, close enough at least!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hmm...?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, I'm looking forward to the Moon-Prayer Night already... We have a festival in Mondstadt called Windblume, and you could always tell which couples are celebrating it for their first time by the smiles on their faces. Big, beaming smiles, like their whole face is glowing.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And I have a feeling we'll get to see that same smile on the Moon Goddess's face at this festival.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Not quite the same, surely...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Anyway, I'll take care of business in the city, but I'll have to leave the decor up to you and the Frostmoon Scions. No one else can capture that traditional aesthetic quite like you guys.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But lastly, there's the final key element that brings the festival to life — companionship.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll take care of that part.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Before you leave, let me show you something that we've been preparing. Mr. Varka had asked to see it already, so you may as well tag along.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...Also, I have some further questions about Kuutar's decision.

choices.text: We've met plenty of them in our time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. What's this? They sure look like they're having fun.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I believe so. Kuuhenki seem very skilled at playing drums like these, although I'm not sure where they learned it from...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Maybe it's an innate talent? In their eyes, they're probably just playing with toys.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Luonnotar! You wanna play too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guess not...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah... She looks more confused than anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we can teach her next time if we get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let's talk here. To tell the truth, I am very surprised to hear that Kuutar is willing to participate in the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I once asked her if she'd be willing to stay with the Frostmoon Scions. I could introduce her to everyone, and we could be a family to one another.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: She did not answer, but she has not appeared here since.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I took this to mean her answer was "no," but if that were the case, she would not have accepted this invitation...

choices.text: Speaking of answers, she asked us to pass along a message:

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Ah...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I see... Maybe she is right. Maybe the Frostmoon Scions of today no longer need a Moon Goddess.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But my wish was not for her to come here and be worshiped as a deity. I simply wanted to offer her a place to stay.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I'm sure she believes that showing herself here might invite Fatui intervention, and as such, she does not wish to cause us trouble.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But what really pains me about all this is that... This is her birthplace, she ought to belong here, yet no one has been able to grant her shelter.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I think I'm qualified to weigh in here... When someone's about to depart on a long trip, what they need is blessings, not burdens. We should wish her the best, not make the journey harder than it already is.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Anyway, she's agreed to attend, hasn't she? All we need to do is simply respect her decision.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I see your point... Yes, she will soon depart, after all.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Our job is to leave her with some happy memories. Besides, who's to say her journey to the moon is a one-way trip? It's not like she can't come back and visit if she wants, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon agrees wholeheartedly! Festivals are all about having fun, so let's keep it simple!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Alright, I'm gonna head back to Nasha Town soon. Wanna come with? I'm guessing you have some other folks to visit there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing, let's go. Bye for now, Lauma!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Thank you all. Goodbye.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (A traveler needs blessings, not burdens...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It sounds good in principle. But will blessings alone be enough for Columbina?)

choices.text: There is no need.

talks.objective: Return to Nasha Town together with Varka

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hey, over there... It's Durin and Albedo with Flins. What could they be chatting about?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Your guess is as good as mine.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: #Ah, Grand Master. And {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hello there. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Perfect, we have some new volunteers for our investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, what investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, let me guess... The righteous Lightkeepers are finally ready to hunt down the Abyssal dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Haha. Yes, that too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, right! Uh... Wait, why does everyone keep saying "that too"?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Well, to be precise, the facts match, but not the causality.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Wait, so I guessed right!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Half right! Don't act so impressed with yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Um, maybe I can explain... We ran into Mr. Flins north of Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: At that time, we'd just noticed a few Abyssal creatures out in the wild, but the strange thing was... I didn't detect any traces of Abyssal energy on them at all.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: On closer inspection, we realized that they were not real monsters, but something akin to reflections in the water... or perhaps a mirage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? Like, you could see them but not touch them?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Exactly. It was very peculiar. They roared and tried to attack us, but we could not make any physical contact with them.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I think I've heard of things like that happening in Nod-Krai before... but I don't know much about it.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Yes, it's a known phenomenon. Mirage-like illusions tend to appear in Nod-Krai in the run-up to Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: From a distance, they appear quite real.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I myself thought that Misters Durin and Albedo were locked in battle with Abyssal monsters when I first arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But after sharing intel and investigating a little further, we can confirm that these illusions are harmless. There is no great cause for concern.

choices.text: I see.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm. All the mirage stories I've heard are either animals, rocks, or small houses. Abyssal monsters, though? That's a first.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It's a first for me, too, so I'm planning to look into it further just to be on the safe side. I intend to inspect a few more locations.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: What about you two? Any plans?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Alice contacted me a few days ago. She'd like me and Durin to assist her with an experiment.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But we lost contact shortly after receiving the message. I'm sure that comes as no surprise to anyone familiar with her.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: We don't know when the wind will blow, yet when the wind blows, we will know. That, in a nutshell, describes how Alice operates.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. That tracks.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Okay. Well, I suggest we investigate this mirage business in the meantime. It's piqued my curiosity, and I'm pretty sure I know someone who will already be ten steps ahead of us.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hah, well said.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? Whatever's happening in Nod-Krai, she always seems to be the first one to know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go see what she knows. We can invite her and her staff to the festival while we're at it.

choices.text: I'm glad that they weren't real.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're right, I have noticed. There's certainly something a little fishy about this situation. Only a little, though.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Records indicate that this phenomenon can occur in the days before and following Moon-Prayer Night. That said, it has always been a rare sight in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The odds of encountering these phantoms are similar to looking up in the night sky, happening to see a shooting star, and managing to make a wish before it disappears.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But this time... either everyone's getting lucky, or they're appearing far more frequently than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Jahoda's out gathering intel as we speak. In the meantime, let me check off some points of interest.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: First, the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: The ones we saw seemed to be Abyssal monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Indeed. But we have identified one location where many more of them have made an appearance. And not just monsters, but human phantoms, too.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Given the scale and nature of the phantoms, it's almost as if... someone's last memories are coming to life. Or perhaps the memories of multiple people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: So you mean, the phantom monsters are hunting down the phantom humans?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Exactly. The phantoms can interact with each other, but we have no means of intervening.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In addition, some of the human phantoms would seem to be from the very distant past. This is clear both from the clothing they wear and the stories they tell.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: They claim to be from Hyperborea — a name which I've heard from Lauma before. If this is true, it means they must be from 6,000 years ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did Paimon hear that right? Six thousand years!?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It sounds like this merits further exploration.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That'd be a big help. I'll leave it with you, Albedo — my knowledge of ancient history is non-existent. I used to doze off every time the pre-Knights of Favonius era came up in class...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It's quite a miracle that you were able to understand these phantoms' speech, given how long ago they lived.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I suppose you're right. But I'll leave the archaeologists to ruminate over that conundrum. As an intelligence broker, my sole interest is in the value of the information I gather.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Which, in this case, hopefully means earning myself some good favor with our dear Lady Moonchanter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So calculating... This intel broker logic always catches Paimon by surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sounds to me like we can split the work up.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I think the Abyssal phenomenon is best left to Albedo, Flins, and me.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Agreed. It coincides with my duty as a Lightkeeper.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: For my part, I'd like to understand the Abyss better. Even a little knowledge would go a long way.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This is certainly a rare opportunity to study the Abyss. But even rarer, perhaps, is the chance to make contact with the ancients.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Curatorium will take the lead on investigating the Hyperboreans. We put in the work to learn what we know so far — it seems only fair that we get some quantity of exclusive intel.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That just leaves our trusty team of two unassigned.

choices.text: Seems like it, yeah.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Since you became an Honorary Knight, of course. This was part of my grand plan all along, hahaha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! By the way, we managed to convince Columbina to come to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations. Would you and Jahoda like to join too?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #She agreed to that? Huh. Quite an achievement. Never underestimate {NICKNAME}, I guess.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I'd be happy to join. No point shutting myself inside when the streets are all decked out. I doubt any clients will be visiting during the festival in any case.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And Jahoda loves a party, so I'm sure she'll jump at the opportunity.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: No, no, no no nonononono...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Tsk, way to contradict me in front of—

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Wait, no! That's not what I... I have bad news, Boss!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: So many people... Alright, everyone inside, quick!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: This is gonna sound crazy, but hear me out... I saw one of those phantoms at Starsand Shoal, and it was... it was some sorta... flying ship!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like a spaceship!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A spaceship at Starsand Shoal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's gotta be the one you came to Teyvat in. You said you saw the same thing through the Moon Marrow, right?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Huh? You already know about it? Ugh... And I thought it was gonna blow people's minds, turns out I'm the last to find out...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Wait, back up! You came here in a spaceship!? Now MY mind is blown. What's it like on the inside? What's it like flying through space? Ahhh, I wanna know everything!

choices.text: M—Maybe that's a conversation for next time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, exactly! Huuuge discovery! You're the best... uh, second-best intel-broker in the world! After your boss, of course.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: W—Wow, really? Hehe, well, I dunno if I'm all that, but...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I guess that decides where we're heading next.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Come on, don't look at me like that. I know the spaceship doesn't have anything to do with me, but... You don't wanna leave me as the only one twiddling my thumbs, do you? ...Please?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, fair enough. You can tag along.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: In that case, let's meet back here to discuss our findings once we're done.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I wish everyone a productive investigation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You too!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: *sigh*

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: What's up, Boss? Aren't we gonna head out?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Tell me, Jahoda. When did the Curatorium start giving out intel for free?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Oh, uh... S—Sorry, Boss!

choices.text: This is still a huge discovery on your part.
Wait, we're a team? Since when?

talks.objective: Go to the spaceship phantom's location

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, whaddya know? Jahoda was right on the money. This phantom really is your spaceship...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But that's so weird. Why would it show up here? Is it some kind of projection? Or... a ghost? Like, maybe it no longer exists, but somehow it left an afterimage...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not sure either...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah, you're already here.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Miss Lauma, what a surprise. I thought you were busy with festival preparations?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I was, until one of our people informed me that a strange sight had appeared at Starsand Shoal.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: No one's ever seen something quite like this before. I thought I should see it for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Same here! Oh — so, we heard that these things appear around the festival period. Any idea why that is?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Unfortunately not. We have very limited information about them, since they can't be interacted with, and no human phantoms have ever made an appearance before now.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The most we've been able to deduce is that these sightings appear to be connected to the increase in kuuvahki energy around this time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's look around and see what we can find out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Seems like that's all we can do. This is all so confusing.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Allow me to lend you a hand.

talks.objective: Seek help from the animals together with Lauma

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Everyone, our friend here should be able to provide us with some information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that.... a phantom Rimehorn Deer...?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I've heard about how the Frostmoon Scions live in harmony with the animals, and can even communicate with them. That's coming in handy now, for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Okay... yes, I understand... Then, how about this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's leaving...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It appears to share our curiosity about this giant spaceship, so I asked it if it wouldn't mind investigating along with some friends.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: In return, I told it about some nearby spots where the wild fruit grows abundantly.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: We may live in a different era from these phantoms, but I trust that the terrain, climate, and ecology here are more resistant to the effects of time than some things are.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let's give them a moment, and hope for the best.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a few moments, the Rimehorn Deer and its companions return happily.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: All back together? Must've been a lot of fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Indeed. Now let me ask them some questions...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It did find a lot of wild fruit, enough for them to feast for a long while.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This puffin circled in the air several times, but didn't spot anything out of the ordinary. Certainly nothing to do with the spaceship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Well, it definitely makes sense to get a bird's eye view.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Indeed. Other than that, I was also thinking that the world these phantoms see is also different from ours.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Oh, I get what you mean. The "wild fruit" exist in both times and spaces, but there might also be things that only exist in that space-time, which we can't see.

choices.text: Because we don't see their whole world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good point... Great thinking, Lauma!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Blunthorn Rhinos can use kuuvahki to shift great rocks, but this one says it couldn't get that ship to budge by even an inch.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The Sniffer Mole tried too. But despite being a skilled digger, it could not get through.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: They say that the spaceship looks robust and undamaged. It seems completely impervious to any and all attacks. Whatever lies within is well-defended from harm.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So, just like us humans, there was nothing they could do about this spaceship either.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Yes. Still, they deserve our thanks.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: We are grateful for all your efforts, dear friends. Now go, and enjoy your feast.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I've noticed some other human phantoms gathered nearby. C'mon. Let's go talk to them.

choices.text: We only see small fragments.

talks.objective: Join Varka in communicating with the phantoms

dialogues.speaker: Kielo
dialogues.text: What is this thing? I've never seen it move, and there's no way to get inside.

dialogues.speaker: Kettu
dialogues.text: Goodness knows. My grandpa says it's been sitting here at least since his grandpa was still alive.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: What about his grandpa? Did he say anything to your grandpa's grandpa about it?

dialogues.speaker: Kettu
dialogues.text: Huh? Um... I don't know. In all likelihood, it was here back then too. Hard to imagine something this huge could move.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Guess that means that as far as they're concerned, this ship's been around a long time.

talks.objective: Join Varka in communicating with the phantoms

dialogues.speaker: Darimir
dialogues.text: Come on, brothers! If we can get even a small chunk off of this thing, it's gotta be worth a fortune! Today is the day we strike it rich!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...? Y—You mean Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yes, brother! I shall join you! Let's make our fortune!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...We should go with them.

dialogues.speaker: Darimir
dialogues.text: What the... This thing is crazy tough, I can't even scratch it. What's it made of!?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sorry, brother... Looks like we'll have to seek our fortunes elsewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Enjoying yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I was just seeing if I could influence this phantom's perception by playing — but nope. No dice.

talks.objective: Discuss the situation with your companions

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm sure we're all starting to build up an idea of what's going on here now that we've spoken to some of the people.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: These phantoms are reenacting real, historical events in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's almost like we're in some kind of interactive stage play. We can talk to the actors, but the plot is fixed, and we can't influence it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It makes sense. History is set in stone. The objective facts of the past cannot be changed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon totally thought you were just goofing around earlier... But actually, you were doing some serious investigating.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Of course I was. Anyway, at this point, I think we're forced to conclude that although the phantom spaceship is right there in front of us, we aren't gonna learn much about it from these people.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(If only this showed the moment when my {M#sister}{F#brother} was searching for me. Maybe then, I could've discovered why {M#she}{F#he} wasn't in the spaceship...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Or, if it showed the moment when it disappeared, I might've found out who was piloting it, and where they were headed...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But no such luck. All we've seen is an arbitrary moment in time during its long stay here.)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Don't be discouraged. If nothing else, this is proof of the ship's existence.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And think about it. So many people tried to hack their way inside, but no one could get the door open. It's made of very tough material.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: To me, that says that we'll either find the ship itself, or the story behind it — it's just a matter of time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, Varka.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, every now and then, when Varka gets serious, he actually does seem like Grand Master material for once...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I wonder how the others are doing... Let's head back for now.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sounds good. Also, drinks are on me if Team Knights of Favonius is the first to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, we have a team name now...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Am I in "Team Knights of Favonius" as well?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You're very welcome to join. We've even got a cathedral ready for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that technically blasphemy? You wouldn't dare make a joke like that if Barbatos was in earshot...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Nah, I'm sure Barbatos doesn't mind a little harmless blasphemy once in a while.

talks.objective: Try to make contact with the phantom in this area

dialogues.speaker: Satatieto
dialogues.text: Help!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh no! Get away!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Satatieto
dialogues.text: Aaaaaaggghhh!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I know it's hard to stomach, Mr. Durin. But as I'm sure you've noticed, there is nothing we can do to intervene in that which unfolds before us.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: *panting* But... we have to at least try...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And try you have. But are you aware of how many unsuccessful attempts you've made now?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Uh... I wasn't keeping count...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'm afraid this is the thirty-ninth failure so far. Or the fifth, if we're only counting this particular victim.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: There are no indications that these phantoms may be altered in any way.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You seem to have calmed down a little.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I'll make us a fire. You should rest and have some water.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Feeling any better now, Mr. Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...May I ask a few questions?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What exactly are we witnessing here? What happened to those people?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: My guess would be that we are seeing Nod-Krai during the Khaenri'ahn Cataclysm. Would that be accurate?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Khaenri'ah...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: As you know, once the Abyss senses even the tiniest crack, it floods in and spreads like wildfire.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: There was a time in the distant past when it permeated all of Nod-Krai, causing immeasurable harm. The people paid a terrible price to heal this land.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Then, five hundred years ago, the whole of Teyvat suffered an Abyssal disaster. Once more, Nod-Krai was dealt a devastating blow.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: In the face of the Abyssal onslaught, all were like grains of sand tossed around by a tidal wave, be they human, fae, or god.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The moment you witnessed is but one drop in a whole ocean of catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Alright... I guess that answers my second question, too. I wanted to know why there's nothing I could do to help them — and that's because what we are seeing is history.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That would be my guess as well.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As I understand it, history and fate are not all that dissimilar. The latter may be unseen to us, but both are immutable.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Yes, fate was determined long, long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I still have a couple of other questions for you, Mr. Flins...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You mentioned more than one Abyssal disaster that has struck this land in the past. How can you be sure that what we're seeing is from the Khaenri'ahn incident?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: And also... how are you able to stay so calm when you're talking about these events?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: From everything I know about you, you're not cold or ruthless, and you're not indifferent to the suffering of others...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmph... Alas, I am forced to show my age. I must be six or seven hundred years old by human measure.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wait... So you...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: One is not easily moved by history when one has witnessed the truth firsthand.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You needn't apologize. Your passion is a good thing to have. Treasure it, because someday, you may find it in terribly short supply.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Now, at the risk of offending you, I have a question in return...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Your curiosity toward the Abyss — is it born from hatred, or because you sense its call?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I only ask because I kept a fragment of Rerir's body in my lantern for a short time — specifically, his heart. So, I know what a burden it can be to carry the Abyss with you.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And I hear its power growling from somewhere within you. In my eyes, your mere existence is a miracle.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My honest answer is... I don't know. I don't think I have the confidence to say for certain. What I will say is, the Abyss is not the only issue that haunts me.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Even before I became who I am today, the question dogged me constantly... should I even exist at all?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My doubts remain unresolved. But... when we fought Rerir, something became a little clearer to me...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Sometimes, it is the darkness within us that allows us to achieve the impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I certainly got the sense from your thirty-nine attempts that you were trying to achieve the impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It sounds like you've resolved to see the truth for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Absolutely. In that sense, he and I are quite similar.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Then I wish you every success. I look forward to the day of your transcension.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Well, if everyone's caught their breath, I suppose we should head back. Oh, and one last thing... I'd appreciate if you kept our discussion about history a secret.

talks.objective: Return to the Curatorium of Secrets to exchange intel

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Incredibly, our separate investigations led us all to the same conclusion. Hooray for consensus.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah, but we barely learned anything though... I totally thought this would be the motherlode! Talking with the ancients? I mean, come on! But nope, all we got was useless snippets of conversation...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: And all this stuff about moons, and "hyberorpea"? What a load of baloney. Seems like people back then had a few screws loose.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I understand your frustration. We found the same issue — each phantom only showed a very brief moment in time.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: There isn't much value to be found in these miscellaneous fragments of a civilization's history, no matter how glorious it may have been.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: If there's a silver lining, it's that these phantoms are harmless to the present reality. They shouldn't get in the way of the festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon agrees! And not just because it's the first thing she understood in this whole conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You look disappointed, Nefer. Is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What do you think? We all worked our tails off, but the only one to gain anything from it was you, Lady Moonchanter.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, please do share the Hyperborean records with me. I will gladly inscribe them in our people's documents.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh, duh, yeah, that was it! Hyperborea, Hyperborea...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm serious. Only an expert in the Frostmoon Scions and their history can turn these records into valuable research material.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The alternative is to let them gather dust on the Curatorium's storage shelves until the pages turn yellow.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Nefer, you're wise enough to know that cooperating and sharing the profits is the best course of action here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, that goes without saying. Sure, let's do that.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh? But didn't you say we aren't supposed to give out intel for free..? Aaah, sorry! Shutting up, shutting up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now is not a good time to push Nefer's buttons...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha. Anyway, back to Moon-Prayer Night. I'm thinking that we should prepare something a little special, aside from the usual decorations and so on.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You mean, a parting gift?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't go wrong with food! Although... Hmm, does food go bad on the moon?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Perhaps a lantern would be a better choice. It might be dark up there.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Mm... It could prove difficult to light a lantern on the moon. Magical stones might serve that purpose better.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: What about a clockwork meka model from Fontaine? I've got a whole bunch at home. I use 'em for fighting practice in my free time!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: None of these sound like things she would be even remotely interested in. But we don't interact with her enough to know what she likes...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah. It would really save us the guesswork if someone could find out what she's into.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wait, what the... Uh, {NICKNAME}, they're all looking at you!

choices.text: Okay, I got it...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Great! Haha, problem solved. Now, I need to stop by Dori's. Gonna need her help sourcing a bunch of stuff for the festival.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #Then let's leave it there for now. We all have our own business to attend to. {NICKNAME} — if you find out what Kuutar likes, let us know right away.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Gotcha.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Is something the matter?

choices.text: That's my line, Durin.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Ah, I'm fine. It's just... I'm still feeling a little rattled after witnessing the horrors of the Abyss.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: But it's okay. This is something I have to work through... I'll be alright. Thanks for your concern.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, don't put too much pressure on yourself. If you ever feel like something's wrong, physically or mentally, we're here to talk.

choices.text: Don't forget, I'm a member of the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hah, come on, stop treating me like a kid.

choices.text: You can always rely on me.
You seem a little down.
I'll find a chance to ask her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone seems hard at work...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They are preparing items for Moon-Prayer Night. For instance, the sculpture being made over here. Mr. Varka and I were just finalizing the details of where it will be placed.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ah, there she is. I didn't know the finished article would be so large...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Not to worry, though, all the necessary arrangements have been made. Just let me know once it's ready, and I'll get some people to ship it over.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You have my thanks. And over here, we are preparing a very traditional confection.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, look at all these colors. It looks great! Can Paimon try one?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hehe, of course. I have a feeling you'll like it a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet! Sweets and treats are Paimon's favorite!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, if you included those in the Feast of the Moon, I bet Paimon would have joined the Frostmoon Scions by now.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: There will also be Verdant Crests like this present in Nasha Town during the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The timing of Moon-Prayer Night is not completely set in advance. We make a rough estimate, then observe the changes in the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms to guide us.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As such, the wait itself is a fun feature of this particular festival.

dialogues.speaker: Kari
dialogues.text: Moon-Prayer Night's nearly here! Hehe, candy, here we come!

dialogues.speaker: Ina
dialogues.text: Don't go feeding all the candy to the animals...

dialogues.speaker: Kari
dialogues.text: I—I wasn't gonna!

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: We're fully focused on festival preparations at the moment. So far, it's all going well.

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Please have patience. The Moon-Prayer Night will soon be upon us.

dialogues.speaker: Sarakka
dialogues.text: This Moonveil doesn't seem translucent enough...

dialogues.speaker: Sarakka
dialogues.text: I think I should take it down and work on it some more.

dialogues.speaker: Wecksell
dialogues.text: The frame is done, and I've got a nice new set of tools. Yep, this is looking good.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We can't unshare information, any more than water spilled on sand can be put back in the bucket. I'll just have to balance the books some other way...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Please, Boss, there's gotta be another way... Who knows — depending on what they find, maybe this will work in our favor, hehe... Please don't fine me, pleeease!

dialogues.speaker: Veikko
dialogues.text: Have you ever seen anything like this?

dialogues.speaker: Mielitty
dialogues.text: Nope. Never seen or heard anything this weird...

dialogues.speaker: Kuuti
dialogues.text: Those illusions, and those people... It's all a little creepy, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Ilmatar
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Nah, all part of the festive atmosphere!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Goodbye for now. I look forward to the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You won't snitch on us, will you?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I'm not entirely sure what you're talking about. But rest assured, I protect client and adventurer confidentiality as a matter of principle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, that's a relief... Paimon does not wanna get an earful from her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since she's agreed to join the festival, let's go see who else wants to take part.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lauma's gotta be the person most familiar with the Moon-Prayer Night. We should start with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, what exactly is your plan to keep her safe?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not sure yet. I'll figure something out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Are you serious!? And Paimon even gave you her vote of confidence back there... When did you become so sneaky?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are these floaty things?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Moonveils. We hang them from buildings in the city during the festival. When you look at the sky through them, it creates a lovely misty effect.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They are the Verdant Crests. When the Night of Moon-Prayer descends, their branches unfurl from crescent to full moon, bathed in divine grace.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: That's also when the grandest celebration of the night begins.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You could say, that's when the feast starts.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The timing of Moon-Prayer Night is not completely set in advance. We make a rough estimate, then observe the changes in the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms to guide us.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As such, the wait itself is a fun feature of this particular festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmm... smells wonderful! Are these for the festival too?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes, they're all traditional desserts of the Frostmoon Children. I'm sure they'll suit your taste, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet! Sweets and treats are Paimon's favorite!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, if you included those in the Sacred Feast, I bet Paimon would have joined the Frostmoon Scions by now.
